# Results — Study 833 (Deflated Sharpe Ratio): the trap, measured

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). This is a **research-method demo**
(Bailey & López de Prado, 2014): run `N` **independent** strategies on a tape with **zero** true
edge, watch the *best* sample Sharpe inflate with `N` exactly as the expected-maximum-Sharpe
formula predicts, then let the **Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR)** shrink that winner back to a coin
flip — while sparing an honestly-good single strategy. The whole study is offline and
deterministic; the "tape" is a seeded null simulation, so there is nothing real to find on the
Signal axis by construction. As-of **2026-06-30** (a dated-run label for parity with the desk;
no market data is used). Fingerprint `f7e4b81df8a2` (null sim: N=1000, T=1260, ann-vol=15%,
seed 833); as-of 2026-06-30.*

## Sim stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| NULL world | an `(T × N)` matrix of **independent, true-zero-edge** strategies — iid `N(0, σ²)` daily returns, σ = 15%/√252, **zero drift** (population Sharpe = 0 in every column) |
| Headline size | **N = 1,000** trials × **T = 1,260** trading days (≈ 5 years), seed 833 |
| Positive control | a single honest strategy: daily returns with a genuine drift set so the *population* annualised Sharpe = **1.0** (not the survivor of a search) |
| Formula | E[max SR] ≈ √V · [ (1−γ)·Z⁻¹(1−1/N) + γ·Z⁻¹(1−1/(N·e)) ], γ = Euler-Mascheroni, V = cross-trial variance of the per-period SR estimates (theory ≈ 1/(T−1)) |
| Correction | DSR = Φ( (SR−SR0)·√(T−1) / √(1 − g₃·SR + (g₄−1)/4·SR²) ), SR0 = E[max SR] over N; at N=1 the DSR is the Probabilistic Sharpe Ratio vs 0 |
| Execution / costs | the winner is priced out-of-sample (first-half IS champion, second-half OOS); the timer charges 2 sides × one-way × NAV/day |
| Independence | trials are **independent by construction** — the pure form the E[max] formula assumes; the correlated crossover-grid version lives in [344](../../344-backtest-overfitting/) |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** N/A: there is no real cross-section, no membership
list. The Signal axis is `NONE` *by construction* — the tape is a certified null, so no real edge
can (or does) exist. A synthetic-only method demo can never earn `REAL`.

## The headline — the best of 1,000 EMPTY strategies

Every one of the 1,000 columns has a *true* Sharpe of exactly zero. Yet the winner dazzles:

| quantity | value | reading |
|---|--:|---|
| mean column Sharpe (the truth) | **+0.03** | ≈ 0 — nothing real, as built |
| **observed max Sharpe** (annualised) | **+1.25** | "a gorgeous backtest" |
| expected max under the null, SR0 | **+1.46** | the bar luck alone clears (N=1000) |
| cross-trial SR dispersion √V | 0.0272 | matches theory 1/√(T−1) = 0.0282 |

The best of 1,000 empty strategies posts an annualised Sharpe of **1.25** — and it is, with
certainty, nothing. In fact it sits *below* the +1.46 the formula says the luckiest of 1,000
nulls should reach, so it is not even impressive **for a search of this size**.

## The deflation — the DSR of that winner

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| winner annualised Sharpe | **+1.25** |
| expected-max bar SR0 (annualised) | +1.46 |
| deflated **excess** Sharpe (SR − SR0) | **−0.21** |
| **Deflated Sharpe Ratio** | **0.324** |
| naive one-sample *t* | **+2.80** |

The naive *t* of **+2.80** screams "significant"; the **DSR = 0.32** (well below 0.95) says the
opposite — the winner is *consistent with the luck of searching 1,000 times*. The deflated excess
Sharpe is **−0.21**: once you subtract the expected maximum, the edge is gone.

## Out-of-sample collapse — the Mirage laid bare

Pick the in-sample (first-half) Sharpe champion, then watch that same column live (second half):

| leg | Sharpe | inference |
|---|--:|---|
| in-sample | **+1.77** | the backtest you'd have published |
| out-of-sample | **−0.28** | Newey-West *t* = **−0.47** (indistinguishable from 0) |

| timer (OOS) | gross | net | *t* (net) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 bp one-way | −1.65 bps/day | **−3.65 bps/day** | −0.98 |
| 5 bps one-way | −1.65 bps/day | **−11.65 bps/day** | −3.13 |

The gorgeous in-sample Sharpe evaporates the instant you stop peeking, and any friction makes it
bleed. There is, by construction, nothing to harvest.

## The inflation curve — E[max] climbs with N (observed vs formula, 40 seeds/point)

| N | observed best Sharpe (sd) | formula E[max] |
|--:|--:|--:|
| 2 | +0.24 (0.36) | +0.23 |
| 5 | +0.49 (0.26) | +0.53 |
| 10 | +0.70 (0.29) | +0.70 |
| 25 | +0.89 (0.25) | +0.89 |
| 50 | +1.01 (0.17) | +1.02 |
| 100 | +1.15 (0.20) | +1.13 |
| 250 | +1.28 (0.20) | +1.27 |
| 500 | +1.37 (0.15) | +1.37 |
| 1000 | +1.47 (0.13) | +1.46 |

The observed best Sharpe tracks the expected-maximum-Sharpe prediction across three orders of
magnitude in the trial count, while the *true* edge stays pinned at zero. **The trial count
inflates the best Sharpe — confirmed.**

## The controls — the machinery is calibrated

Across **40** independent null pools (N=1,000 each), how often does each screen call the winner
"real"?

| screen | fires | reading |
|---|--:|---|
| naive best-Sharpe & \|*t*\| ≥ 2 | **40/40 (100%)** | manufactures a "discovery" every time |
| **DSR ≥ 0.95** | **0/40 (0%)** | calibrated near the nominal 5% |
| mean DSR of the winner | **0.509** | a coin flip — as it should be |
| mean deflated-excess Sharpe | +0.011 | ≈ 0 — the winner shrunk back to nothing |

**Positive control — an honest single strategy keeps a high DSR** (true Sharpe 1.0, single
hypothesis, 40 seeds): realised annualised Sharpe **+1.01**, **mean DSR 0.965**, DSR ≥ 0.95 in
33/40 seeds. And a genuinely *strong* strategy (true Sharpe 2.0) planted inside the N=1,000 pool
is the pool's winner and still clears the luck bar (DSR **0.648 > 0.5**) even buried among 1,000
trials. The correction punishes *searching*, not *skill* — never cited to support a real-tape
stamp (there is no real tape).

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** By construction. The tape is a certified null; the best of 1,000 empty
  strategies looks like a Sharpe-1.25 winner (naive *t* = +2.80) and is provably nothing. There
  is no real edge to find — a synthetic method demo, capped at NONE on the Signal axis.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The in-sample champion collapses out-of-sample (+1.77 → −0.28,
  NW *t* = −0.47) and bleeds on any cost (−3.65 bps/day net at 1 bp). Nothing to harvest.
- **Does the trial count inflate the best Sharpe? — CONFIRMED.** The observed maximum Sharpe
  tracks the expected-maximum-Sharpe formula from N=2 to N=1,000 (r ≈ 1); the DSR shrinks the
  winner to a coin flip (mean 0.509, deflated excess ≈ 0) and fires on only 0/40 nulls vs 40/40
  for the naive screen — while sparing the honest single strategy (mean DSR 0.965). A Sharpe is
  meaningless without its trial count; the Deflated Sharpe Ratio is how you restore the meaning.
